Things to keep in mind here:

  • You're a temp, presumably an employee of a temp agency.

  • It sounds like your time span with said temp agency is so short that the gap in the resume can't even register as a blip on the radar.

  • I'm assuming you're a decent person, just be upfront with the temp agency and start that new job ASAP assuming everything else about it is better.

  • The extra 20 miles a day on your vehicle is negligible. The extra $2 an hour more than covers for it.

My thoughts:

If you're not job hopping the higher paying job will be worth taking in the long run. If I were in your position I would completely omit the present job from my resume and leave it as a (presumably one month or shorter) gap but even if you don't most employers won't mind that you quit for a higher paying position once. And the higher pay means that you're valued at that higher rate, so future employers will be more likely to hire you and more likely to offer you a higher rate.

Only you know whether it costs less to take the more distant job than you'll be getting. It depends on your cost of transportation and how many hours you're working per trip. 20 extra miles per day isn't nothing. If traffic or travel stresses you out consider that in your choice. Also consider the extra cost of car maintenance and the loss of time.

The company you're working for now won't even care that you're gone. Sorry to break it to you. If you're not a full time directly contracted employee they expect you to leave on a moment's notice. Still you should tell the new place you want w week (or two weeks) notice so you can tell your present employer. That actually makes you look good because it proves you are already valued enough to hire by another company and that you have the decency to give warning before you quit.

There is some risk in moving. If things don't work out at the other factory you could be faced with a combination of a local factory that no longer wants you (your temp agency probably won't care) a longer gap on your resume, and no job.
